newsitem.title: HONG KONG: PRESS DIGEST-Hong Kong Newspaper Headlines-April 3.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST-Hong Kong Newspaper Headlines-April 3.

text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Hong Kong press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

-- MING PAO -- When meeting U.S. House of Representatives speaker Newt Gingrich, Taiwan President Lee Teng-hui expressed the wish to buy more advanced weapons for defence purposes because China has never said it would not invade Taiwan.

-- APPLE DAILY -- China is sending several hundred public security agents to Hong Kong to collect information on major local and foreign organisations, watch the movements of target individuals and prevent separatist activities.
-- TA KUNG PAO -- Chinese Premier Li Peng stressed that the "one country two systems" principle will protect the legal interests of foreign countries in Hong Kong.

-- Chinese Foreign Minister Qian Qichen during a meeting with representatives of Hong Kong's business sector called on Hong Kong people to understand the "one country, two systems" principle and promote it.
-- ECONOMIC TIMES -- Dickson Concept's plan to acquire U.S. retailer Barney's Inc was facing joint competition from two Japanese retail groups.

-- SOUTH CHINA MORNING POST -- The annual U.S. State Department report on Hong Kong said that despite significant positive developments in the territory, China had approached the handover with some "disturbing" acts reversing gains in freedom and civil liberties.

-- Hong Kong was one of the costliest major markets to deal in, according to an operational risk-adjusted index launched by two British groups. Singapore was the costliest in Asia and fourth in the world.

-- HONGKONG STANDARD -- Chief Executive-designate Tung Chee-hwa would leave for the United States early next month to lobby for support of his administration in spite of advice from U.S. politicians that he would be in a "no-win" situation.
